memory_update.text: New Hotspots should remain a cross-sector chokepoint funnel rather than a single-ticker theme, with AI power/grid, sulphuric acid, regulated APIs, refractories, and supplier stress treated as separate nodes.

Transmission hardware and utility structures are currently the highest-priority underfollowed node because PLPC, ACA, VMI, AZZ, MYRG, HUBB, and PWR create a testable chain from EPC backlog to upstream component demand.
Sulphur and sulphuric acid remain a high-priority commodity chokepoint, but public-market mapping must distinguish acid producers/exporters from acid users whose margins may be hurt.
Regulated niche API suppliers should survive Layer 1 only as hypothesis candidates until molecule-level DMF, inspection, customer, export, and margin evidence is verified.

The Layer 1 universe is still too US-grid-heavy; Layer 2 should add non-US listed suppliers in transmission hardware, insulators, cable accessories, testing/inspection, grid software, acid logistics, and smelter-acid exports.

summary: Layer 1C merged universe for New Hotspots. The strongest current node is AI/data-center power transmission hardware and adjacent grid-infrastructure suppliers, led by PLPC as the most direct underfollowed candidate and supported by reference leaders such as HUBB, PWR, and MYRG. Additional breadth is preserved through sulphur/sulphuric-acid disruption beneficiaries and victims, niche regulated API suppliers, Indian refractories, nuclear fuel, and an auto-supplier-stress research seed. Several non-grid nodes remain hypothesis-level because the supplied evidence identifies the chokepoint but not yet enough primary company-level proof.
